sources.citation: Ntumy, Samuel K. 2003 [title page dated 2002]. Sociolinguistic survey in the Jwira language area. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2003-001. Dallas: SIL International. 43 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic survey only (comprehension of Nzema, language use, attitudes, literacy). No phonology section; a full-text search for stress/accent/tone/accent/prosod/syllab hits only a blank community-questionnaire prompt 'forms(pronunciation, vocabulary, tone?)' on p. 29 (Appendix C, item 4). Appendix B wordlist is printed as an empty 200-item gloss template with no Jwira forms. p. 5 gives classification (Kwa, Central Comoe/Tano) and three dialect areas; p. 14 reports 82% assumed cognates with Nzema; section 3 (p. 6) says the only prior work is an unpublished 1989 GILLBT task asses…

sources.citation: Chan, Eugene (compiler). 'Jwira-Pepesa / Pepisa'. In: Numeral Systems of the World's Languages (MPI-EVA Leipzig web database). Data supplied by Mr. Sammy Ntumy, GILLBT (Ghana Institute of Linguistics, Literacy and Bible Translation), 11 April 2002.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No prose on prosody. The numerals carry acute (high-tone) marks on some syllables, e.g. 2 ńwia, 3 ńsa, 4 ńna, 5 ńnu, 6 ńsiã, 7 ńsuw, 8 mɔ́twɛ, 9 nɡhoalá, 10 eburú, 11 burú né ko, 20 aburúnwia, 30 aburásã, 80 aburáwɔ́twɛ, 100 eyaa ko - i.e. tone-marked wordlist data (syllabic nasal prefix marked high, unmarked syllables presumably low), which shows the fieldworker transcribed lexical tone but states nothing about the tone system or stress. Only comment: 'Jwira-Pepesa has a decimal system.'

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page jwir1241 (classification, dialects Jwira [jwir1242] and Pepesa [pepe1238], 'meds' list); Wikipedia 'Jwira-Pepesa language' stub; Wikidata Q35467; ISO 639-3 page for jwi
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Wikipedia stub: two mutually intelligible dialects, 60% intelligibility with Nzema, 'Jwira-Pepesa has no written form', sources Ethnologue and SIL only. Glottolog's subclassification comment cites Ntumy 2003; its 'most extensive descriptions' slots are filled by Nzema dictionaries and Chinebuah 1963, i.e. misassigned Nzema works.
